concerns.text: FR-004 demands Spearman rank-correlation tests that 'MUST control for the length of the generated description as a covariate'. Plain Spearman correlation cannot control for a covariate; the procedure is ambiguous (partial Spearman? residualized ranks? stratified analysis?). An implementer cannot know when this FR is met. Specify the exact statistical procedure (e.g., partial Spearman via rank-regression residuals) or move covariate control exclusively to FR-008's regression.

The tie-breaker rule is uninterpretable: 'select the two original scores closest to the median ... and average them with the third score to produce the final score.' Averaging two scores 'with the third' is not a defined operation, and it conflicts with the earlier clause that the manual score is 'the median of the three normalized scores.' Two different final-score definitions coexist; a test cannot verify both. Pick one deterministic formula.

FR-011 says the manual score is the 'normalized rubric average' while FR-009 defines it as the median of normalized scores (plus the tie-breaker). Reconcile the terminology so the validation metric in FR-011/SC-003 is computed from a single, unambiguously defined quantity.

SC-001/SC-002 name the metric and reference (RAM limit, job limit) but omit the execution conditions needed to measure them — sample size (1000 per US-1 scenario 3) and the pass condition (e.g., completes without OOM-kill / within the 4h stated in US-1). Add the observable pass/fail condition so the criterion is decidable.
